subject: Announcement consent onboarding checklist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Announcement consent onboarding checklist

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. As we prep the final MSA/order form I wanted to surface a short, practical checklist that will make the announcement and logo/reference pieces straightforward for both teams. Our legal team asked that we capture the operational steps so we don’t have to re-negotiate the same small items later.

High-level proposal (attached: MSA_redlines_olga_v1.pdf and a draft annex):
- Annex: "Announcement Process" attached as a lightweight appendix (Announcement_Process_Annex_v2.docx). This covers: embargo window, approval rounds, who signs off (marketing + legal), and allowed logo variations.
- Publicity consent: limited to one joint press release and up to three case study quotes; all marketing assets subject to review within 3 business days.
- Logo use: Acme may use Redwood logo only in the context of the announced solution; vector and color specs supplied by us. Any co-branded material requires mutual sign-off.
- Confidentiality carve-out: mention of the relationship in marketing collateral will not disclose technical architecture, customer data practices, or pricing.
- Exceptions: customer-requested testimonials beyond the three quotes require commercial approval and an updated addendum.

Ask from your side: can you confirm (a) Acme is comfortable with an annex instead of inline MSA language, and (b) a 3-business-day approval turnaround for creative and quotes? If either is a hard stop, flag what turnaround or wording you need and we’ll iterate.

I’ll loop in Marcus (legal lead) to confirm the language if useful.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0183

Attachment: MSA_redlines_olga_v1.pdf (PDF, 32KB)
Attachment: Announcement_Process_Annex_v2.docx (DOCX, 14KB)

From: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 11:20:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Announcement consent onboarding checklist

Olga —

Appreciate the clear checklist and the annex approach looks good in principle. A few items from legal/marketing here: 

1) Approval turnaround: our marketing team typically requires 5 business days for sign-off on external-facing language (brand + legal review). Can Redwood accommodate 5 BD instead of 3?
2) Logo usage: we can accept an annex, but we need a specific allowed usage list (homepage logo, case studies, partner page). Also we will not allow use in paid advertising without separate permission.
3) Confidentiality carve-out: we cannot have any language that says "Redwood may reference Acme publicly" without explicit quote approvals. All quotes must be pre-approved and attributable as drafted by us.

I’ve copied procure@acmeanalytics.com on this thread to keep procurement looped for the order form timing.

If useful, happy to do a 20-min alignment tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Sarah Lowe
Legal & Partnerships
Acme Analytics

Thanks Sarah — that makes total sense. Two quick clarifications and an internal ask: 

- We can extend to 5 business days for standard marketing copy and logo assets. For quick quote approvals (single-sentence customer quotes), would you consider 3 business days if highlighted as "expedited" and agreed in the annex?
- We will add explicit allowed logo locations to the annex (homepage, partner page, case study PDF) and add the paid-ad restriction.

Internal: Marcus / Dev, could you review the attached MSA redlines and the annex and call out any hard stops? In particular: 
- Confidentiality carve-out language that permits mention of the relationship in marketing (we want "Non-sensitive relationship mention allowed with sign-off").
- Mechanism: “two-round review” with timestamps and tie to a single DocuSign sign-off event so procurement can close the deal without waiting for an indefinite number of revisions.

I’ve attached the current redline — Marcus, please mark any legal-required language before EOD tomorrow so we can send an updated annex back to Acme.

Thanks —
Olga

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Announcement consent onboarding checklist

Olga / Dev —

Quick review from legal: overall approach is fine, annex preferred. Key edits I tracked in the redline (see MSA_redlines_olga_v1.pdf):
- Replace "Non-sensitive relationship mention allowed" with "Permitted Marketing References" clause that enumerates allowed content and explicitly excludes any customer data, pricing, or architecture diagrams.
- Approval SLAs: set 5 business days for marketing/legal review, with an "expedited" flag that shortens to 3 BD for single-line customer quotes or logo-only usage; expedited requests must be flagged in subject line and include the asset for review.
- Add a final sentence: "Failure to respond within the stated SLA shall be deemed approval for non-substantive edits only." (this will help procurement close deals).
- Logo files: provide vector + PNG with color and monochrome variants; specify that Redwood will host approved logos on a public CDN for partner access.

Comment for sales: the "deemed approval" clause is negotiable — if Acme pushes back, offer a fixed maximum of one additional expedited review before requiring commercial approval.

I can hop on a 20-min call if you want to walk through the redline with Sarah tomorrow.

—Marcus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
